symptom.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the major depressive episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by a major depressive episode accompanied by delusions and/or hallucinations that occur only during the mood episode. The content of the psychotic features is often mood-congruent (e.g., guilt, worthlessness, somatic or nihilistic themes), and the condition typically causes marked functional impairment and elevated suicide risk. Onset may follow severe psychosocial stressors, medical illness, or recurrent untreated depression, and episodes can be single or recurrent, often more severe and longer in duration than non-psychotic depression. It is differentiated from primary psychotic disorders by the temporal link between mood symptoms and psychosis, and from bipolar disorder by the absence of manic or hypomanic episodes.

patient.personality: Sherly is a meticulous, community‑oriented woman who finds purpose in mentoring others and maintaining structured routines in both her work and home life.
patient.stressor: Two years before presentation, Sherly’s husband died suddenly from a heart attack, and while she initially coped by throwing herself into work and church activities, the first real rupture in her routine came when she downsized to a smaller home and had to clear out his belongings alone. The quiet of the new house, her grown children living out of state, and the approach of her planned retirement made her increasingly preoccupied with fears of being useless and abandoned, and she began spending long evenings poring over old policies and financial documents trying to reassure herself she was secure. Over the following seven months, colleagues noticed she became withdrawn at the office, obsessively re‑checking client files, and she gradually stopped attending choir, skipping community events she once organized, and neglecting her garden as she ruminated at home. She finally sought psychiatric help at the urging of her pastor and a mentee after she started insisting that certain clients and neighbors were secretly trying to strip away her savings and home, despite repeated reassurance and clear evidence to the contrary.
patient.chief_complaint: “I know people are plotting to take everything my husband and I worked for, and no one believes me.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: No matter how many times the bank or my kids or my pastor show me the statements, I am absolutely certain that some of my clients and even my next‑door neighbor are working together behind my back to drain my accounts and force me out of this house, like they’re punishing me for something I must have done wrong with my husband’s money.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: When I’m alone in the evenings, especially in the kitchen or lying in bed, I hear these low, whispering voices that sound like people from church or the office saying things like, “She doesn’t deserve that house,” or “We’ll take it all,” even though no one is actually there and the TV is off.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling like a stone in my chest, and it just sits there all day while I move around the house thinking, “What’s the point, Sherly, everyone’s forgotten you and you’re just waiting to be pushed aside.”

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to look forward to choir rehearsal and tending my roses after work, but now even the thought of going to church or stepping outside to pull a few weeds feels pointless and exhausting, so I just stay inside and shuffle papers or stare at the TV without really watching it.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Over these past months my appetite has just disappeared—I’ll realize it’s late afternoon and I haven’t eaten more than a few crackers or a piece of toast, and even then I have to force it down because food just has no taste and my stomach feels knotted most of the time.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: My body feels like it’s moving through molasses—at the office I find myself just sitting there, staring at the same policy for ten or fifteen minutes before I can make my hand pick up a pen, and when people ask me a simple question, it takes me forever to answer because my thoughts feel stuck.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even on days when I go to bed early and don’t do much more than sit at my desk or on the couch, I feel completely drained, like I’ve run a marathon, and just walking from the bedroom to the kitchen or taking a shower can wear me out so much I have to sit down and rest afterward.
